key_facts: Reported palpitation and amaurosis before loss of consciousness
Previous episode of syncope 1 month prior
Vital signs: blood pressure 125/96 mm Hg, pulse rate 81 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation 99% under ambient air
Normal laboratory tests, including blood glucose, electrolytes, D-dimer, troponin I, and N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide
Abnormal 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and QTc of 403 milliseconds
Coronary Angiography showed 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD and 80% stenosis in mid-right coronary artery

raw.rationale: The patient experienced syncope with preceding palpitation and amaurosis, and the 12-lead 24-hour Holter monitoring recorded polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode, which is consistent with Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (CPVT). The normal QTc interval at rest (403 milliseconds) also supports this diagnosis, as CPVT is characterized by a normal QT interval at rest but can exhibit polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during physical or emotional stress.

rejected.label: Torsades de Pointes
rejected.why: Torsades de Pointes is typically associated with a prolonged QT interval, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Long QT Syndrome
rejected.why: Long QT Syndrome is characterized by a prolonged QT interval, which is not present in this case (QTc of 403 milliseconds).

rejected.label: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation
rejected.why: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation is a diagnosis of exclusion, and the presence of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during a presyncope episode suggests a specific underlying condition, such as CPVT.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy is characterized by right ventricular dysfunction and fibrofatty replacement, which is not evident in the provided information.

rejected.label: Brugada Syndrome
rejected.why: Brugada Syndrome is characterized by a specific electrocardiographic pattern (ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3), which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Short QT Syndrome
rejected.why: Short QT Syndrome is characterized by a shortened QT interval, which is not present in this case (QTc of 403 milliseconds).
